title: GitHub App as the primary auth and install flow
description:
## User Story

As a new user, I want to install TAG on my org from GitHub's install screen, so that TAG has
access to exactly the repositories I chose and I never paste a token.

## Description

TAG can already mint installation tokens from an App id, private key and installation id, but
nothing registers an App, nothing receives the install redirect, and the local instance runs
on a personal token with a typed `GITHUB_REPOS`. App mode should become the primary path:
the App is registered once for the org (by hand, in org settings; the ticket documents the
permissions: Actions read, Pull requests read, Contents read, Metadata read, and write on
Contents and Pull requests if ticket 8's pull requests are opened by the App); TAG serves a
"Install on GitHub" link; GitHub redirects back with `installation_id`; TAG stores it and
lists the installation's repositories, so `GITHUB_REPOS` is not needed in App mode. Token
mode stays as the self-hosted and local path and is documented as such. Sign-in for people
is out of scope here (TAG keeps its password) but the App is registered so OAuth can be added.

## Out of Scope

- OAuth sign-in for users.
- Several installations in one TAG instance.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- With App credentials and no `GITHUB_REPOS`, TAG lists the installation's repositories.
- The install redirect records the installation id without a restart.
- Token mode still works unchanged with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_REPOS`.
- Calls made in App mode count against the installation's rate limit, not a person's.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: first install

**Given** a fresh TAG with App id and private key configured and no installation
**When** the user clicks "Install on GitHub", chooses three repositories, and GitHub redirects
back
**Then** TAG shows those three repositories and starts their backfill

title: Run ingest in the background with a status endpoint
description:
## Description

`POST /api/ingest` holds the request until the whole pass ends (about 40 seconds across four
repositories), and Bun drops an idle connection after 10 seconds, so the button fails while
the pass carries on. The route should start the pass in a background fiber and answer 202
with a pass id at once. A `GET /api/ingest/status` reports the running pass (repositories
done, current one, errors so far) and the last finished one. The page shows "checking…" while
a pass runs, re-fetches as each repository finishes, and shows the summary when it ends. The
255-second idle timeout added to `index.ts` on 2026-10-25 is then removed.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `POST /api/ingest` answers within a second whatever the pass length.
- `GET /api/ingest/status` reports progress per repository and the final summary.
- A repository's new reports appear in the page before the pass over later repositories has
  finished.
- The Bun idle timeout is back at its default.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: check for new runs on a slow org

**Given** four repositories whose pass takes 40 seconds
**When** the user clicks "check for new runs"
**Then** the button shows "checking…", the first repository's new runs appear within its own
share of the pass, and the button returns to normal with the summary when the pass ends
close_reason: Merged to main as 823d357; check green (72 tests)

title: Handle GitHub rate limits and report real HTTP errors
description:
## Description

A 403 from GitHub (secondary rate limit, or a missing scope) is decoded as JSON and fails as
a schema error ("missing key artifacts"), which hid the real cause on 2026-10-25. The client
should fail with the HTTP status and GitHub's `message`, read `x-ratelimit-remaining`,
`x-ratelimit-reset` and `retry-after`, and on 403 or 429 pause the pass until the reset
instead of failing every remaining run. The runs list should send `If-None-Match` so an
unchanged list returns 304, which GitHub does not count against the limit.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A non-2xx answer surfaces as a source error carrying the status and GitHub's message.
- When GitHub answers 403 or 429 with a reset or retry-after, the pass waits until then and
  continues; the pass summary names the wait.
- The runs list sends the last ETag and treats 304 as "no change".

## Scenarios

### Scenario: secondary rate limit mid-pass

**Given** GitHub answers 403 with `retry-after: 30` on the fifth run of a pass
**When** the pass continues
**Then** TAG waits 30 seconds, resumes at the fifth run, and the summary records one wait and
no per-run errors
close_reason: Merged to main as 390fdd5; check green (68 tests)

title: List a repository's artifacts in one call and remember seen runs
description:
## Description

A pass calls `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/artifacts` once per run, in
series, for the 20 newest completed runs, and repeats this every pass even though a completed
run never gains artifacts. That is about 25 calls and 9 seconds per repository with nothing
to download. GitHub also offers `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/artifacts`, which lists a
repository's artifacts newest first, 100 a page, each with its run id, branch and commit.

The pass should list a repository's artifacts with that call, ingest only runs it has not
seen, and record each run once its artifacts are in the index (a `runs_seen` table). Runs
within a pass may be worked a few at a time. Two passes must not overlap: a second request
waits for the first.

Partly written and unchecked in `ingest.ts`, `result-store.ts` (2026-10-25); the per-run
call is still in place.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A steady-state pass over a repository with no new runs makes one artifacts call and no
  per-run calls.
- A run whose artifacts have been indexed is not listed again on later passes.
- An artifact that was listed but never cached (download failed) is retried on a later pass.
- Two concurrent ingest requests run one after the other.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: second pass is cheap

**Given** a repository whose 20 newest runs were ingested on the previous pass
**When** a pass runs with no new completed runs
**Then** TAG makes one artifacts list call for the repository and no run-level calls

### Scenario: a failed download is retried

**Given** an artifact row in state `listed` because its download failed
**When** the next pass runs
**Then** TAG downloads it again without re-listing the run

title: Split the eleven source files over 500 lines
description:
## Description

AGENTS.md now holds a 500-line limit per source file, enforced by bun run file-length with a baseline (scripts/file-length-baseline.json) that lists the files already over it. Split each of those files into modules of one concern, keep the original module path as the entry point that re-exports what importers use so no import site changes, and drop the file from the baseline. Three disjoint batches so they can run in parallel without touching the same files:

- server: packages/app/src/server/result-store.ts (909), github-source.ts (710), ingest.ts (608), http.ts (595)
- web: packages/app/src/grouping.ts (1036), packages/app/src/web/home.tsx (971), packages/app/src/web/main.tsx (613)
- ui and tests: packages/ui/src/groups.tsx (653), packages/ui/src/data.tsx (504), packages/app/test/github-source.test.ts (927), packages/app/test/ingest.test.ts (541)

## Acceptance Criteria

- bun run check passes with the split files removed from the baseline.
- No behaviour change: the same tests pass unchanged except for import paths within the test files themselves.
- Each new module is under 500 lines and holds one concern named in its first comment.
close_reason: All eleven files split under the 500-line limit across PRs 3, 4 and 5; the baseline is empty

title: Suggest lockstep release groups and collections
description:
## Description

Releases across repositories sit as separate rows on the org releases section, and
collections exist only if typed. After backfill TAG can detect patterns and suggest, never
create: tags with the same name across two or more repositories within a day on most of
their recent releases (a lockstep release group); environments named like production; tags
that parse as semver; scheduled workflows; failing on the default branch across the org.
Each suggestion shows the query or group it would save and a yes saves it, a no dismisses
it. A saved release group is a stored record (org, repositories, rule "same tag name") and
the org releases section then shows one row per version with the repositories underneath.
Repositories that release alone keep their own rows.

## Out of Scope

- Creating any collection or group without a yes.
- Match rules other than "same tag name".
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Two repositories tagging v1.4.0 and v1.3.2 within a day of each other are suggested as a
  release group; a repository tagging on its own cadence is not.
- Accepting the suggestion makes the org releases section show one row per version with a
  verdict per repository.
- Dismissed suggestions do not return unless the data changes.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: lockstep pair

**Given** provenance and provenance-web both tagged v1.4.0 and v1.3.2 a few hours apart
**When** the org page loads after backfill
**Then** a suggestion names the two repositories and the shared tags, and accepting it shows
v1.4.0 as one row with both repositories' verdicts
close_reason: PR 8 merged: lockstep release groups and collection suggestions with accept and dismiss

title: Onboarding page: install, repos, first report
description:
## User Story

As a new user, I want one page that takes me from install to my first report, so that I know
what to do next at every step.

## Description

A first-run page that shows: the install link (ticket 4) until an installation exists; then
each installed repository with its scan state (ticket 7): `reporting` with backfill progress
(ticket 6), `needs-change` with a "propose pull request" action (ticket 8) and then the PR's
state, `unsupported` with what was found, `no-tests`. When the first report lands the page
says so with the number of tests and links to the repository page. Retention is stated as a
sentence with its default, not a form. After onboarding the page is reachable from the rail
for adding repositories.

## Out of Scope

- Status checks, notifications, team invites, collections: after the first report.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A user with no installation sees only the install step.
- Each repository shows exactly one of the four states and the action that state needs.
- The first ingested report is announced with its test count and a link.
- Nothing on the page needs typing.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: three repositories, mixed

**Given** an installation with one reporting repository, one needing a change, one with no
tests
**When** the onboarding page loads
**Then** the first shows backfill progress, the second shows "propose pull request", the third
says no tests were found, and no field asks for input
close_reason: PR 11 merged: the onboarding page at #/onboarding with the install step, each repository's state and action, the first report, the retention sentence and the rail link

title: Propose the CI change as a pull request
description:
## User Story

As a new user whose repository needs a CI change, I want TAG to open the pull request for
me, so that onboarding is a review and a merge, not an edit.

## Description

For a `needs-change` repository, TAG generates the change made by hand on 2026-10-25 for
hyperstition, provenance and provenance-web: the runner's JUnit (or CTRF) reporter flag or
config, and an `actions/upload-artifact` step with `if: always()` after the test step. The App
opens a pull request on a branch named for TAG, with a description that says what it adds
and why. The generator is a pure function from the scan result and the workflow text to the
new workflow text, so it is testable on fixtures. The PR's own CI run uploads the artifact,
and TAG ingests pull request runs, so the first report lands while the PR is open. If the App
lacks write permission the page offers the diff to copy instead.

## Out of Scope

- Editing existing reporter config beyond adding the JUnit output.
- Runners the scan does not recognise.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- For each runner found, the generated workflow runs it with a JUnit output and uploads it
  with `if: always()`; the existing steps are otherwise unchanged.
- The pull request is opened by the App with the generated change and a plain description.
- The pull request's first CI run produces an artifact that TAG ingests.
- Without write permission, the same diff is shown for copying and no PR is attempted.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: vitest and playwright

**Given** a `needs-change` repository with vitest and playwright jobs
**When** the user accepts the proposal
**Then** a pull request appears with a JUnit reporter on both and two upload steps, its CI run
uploads both, and TAG shows both reports against the pull request before it is merged
close_reason: PR 10 merged: the CI change generator, App pull-request writes, the proposal API and panel, and the copy-the-diff fallback

title: Detect test runners and existing report artifacts
description:
## User Story

As a new user, I want TAG to tell me what my repository already produces and what it would
need, so that I do not read docs to find out.

## Description

Onboarding needs to classify each repository without the user's help. Two signals, both from
data rather than guesses:

1. Existing artifacts: from the repository's artifacts list, group by artifact name, download
   one sample per name, and run the adapters on it. A name that yields reports means the
   repository already reports. Names that hold test output TAG does not read yet (mocha JSON,
   TAP, go test JSON) are named so the user knows why they do not count.
2. Test runners: from the tree and workflow files, detect vitest, jest, bun test, playwright,
   mocha, cargo test and nextest, pytest, go test, deepeval; and for each, the workflow job
   and command that runs it.

Also read the default branch and the environments from the repository API, replacing the
guess from run history. The scanner is a pure function over a file tree and workflow text so
it is testable without GitHub. Result per repository: `reporting` (with artifact names),
`needs-change` (with the runners and jobs found), `unsupported` (with what was found), or
`no-tests`.

## Out of Scope

- New adapters for formats found by the scan; they become their own tickets, ordered by how
  often the scan meets them.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A repository that uploads a JUnit or CTRF artifact under any name is classified
  `reporting` and no CI change is proposed.
- A repository with vitest and playwright in a GitHub workflow is classified `needs-change`
  naming both runners and the job that runs them.
- The default branch shown in TAG matches the repository's setting on GitHub.
- The scanner runs on fixture trees in tests without network.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: already reporting

**Given** a repository whose CI uploads `test-results-ubuntu-latest` holding a nextest JUnit
file
**When** it is scanned
**Then** it is classified `reporting` and the sample report is ingested

### Scenario: tests but no reports

**Given** a repository with `pnpm vitest` in a workflow job named "Tests" and no report
artifact
**When** it is scanned
**Then** it is classified `needs-change` with runner `vitest`, job "Tests", and the command

title: Per-repository backfill with visible state
description:
## Description

The first pass takes a fixed 20 runs. A repository that already uploads reports has history
worth showing, bounded by the retention window. On first sight of a repository TAG should
walk its artifacts list (ticket 1) back until an artifact's run is older than the retention
window or the list ends, ingesting as it goes, and show the repository as soon as the first
page has landed. Each repository carries a state: `new`, `backfilling` (with runs done and
seen so far), `current`. The repository header on the scope page shows backfill progress
and the overview shows which repositories are still backfilling. Backfill runs in the
background pass (ticket 3).
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A newly installed repository with a year of artifacts ends up with every run inside the
  retention window and none outside it.
- The repository page is usable while backfill continues and shows "backfilling, N of M".
- Backfill resumes after a restart from where it stopped.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: long history

**Given** a repository with 400 completed runs that upload reports, and 30-day retention
**When** it is installed
**Then** the repository appears within seconds showing its newest runs, the header shows
backfill progress, and when it ends only runs from the last 30 days are indexed
close_reason: Backfill with visible state landed on main

title: Ingest on workflow_run events with a poll as backstop
description:
## User Story

As a user, I want a finished CI run to show in TAG without clicking anything, so that TAG is
current when I look.

## Description

Nothing runs ingest on a schedule; new runs appear only after a click or a restart. With the
App installed and subscribed to `workflow_run`, TAG receives a `completed` event with the
run id. The handler verifies the `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC with the webhook secret, answers
200 at once, and queues the run durably (SQLite). A worker ingests queued runs one at a time
per repository: one artifacts call, download, adapters. A slow poll with conditional requests
(ticket 2) runs every ten minutes as a backstop for missed deliveries, and the manual button
stays. In token mode there is no webhook, so the poll is the only path.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A valid `workflow_run.completed` delivery results in that run's reports within a minute.
- A delivery with a bad signature is rejected with 401 and nothing is queued.
- A queued run survives a restart and is ingested after it.
- A run missed by the webhook is picked up by the next poll.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: run completes

**Given** TAG is installed on a repository and subscribed to workflow_run
**When** a workflow run with a test report artifact completes
**Then** TAG answers the delivery with 200 within a second and the run's report is in the
index within a minute

### Scenario: delivery lost

**Given** GitHub failed to deliver an event for a completed run
**When** the next poll runs
**Then** the run is ingested and marked seen
close_reason: PR 9 merged: workflow_run webhook with a durable queue, a worker, and a ten-minute poll backstop

title: Frictionless GitHub onboarding
description:
## User Story

As someone who runs CI on GitHub, I want to install TAG and see my test results without
editing config or CI by hand, so that TAG is useful within minutes of installing it.

## Description

Today TAG reads GitHub with a personal token and a typed repository list, lists every run's
artifacts on every pass, holds the HTTP request open for the whole pass, and shows nothing
until someone has changed the repository's CI to upload a test report. This epic turns that
into: install the GitHub App, pick repositories, let TAG detect what the repository already
produces, propose the one CI change where it is needed, and show the first report while the
proposing pull request is still open. New runs arrive by webhook.

## Out of Scope

- Status checks, notifications, and team invites: after the first report lands.
- Any configuration knob not already in the environment (auth mode, repos in token mode,
  retention days).
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A new user goes from install to a first ingested report without typing a token, a
  repository name, or a CI change.
- A completed workflow run appears in TAG within a minute of finishing, without a click.
- One ingest pass costs at most a handful of GitHub calls per repository in steady state.
